rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creature’s apparent guardianship is not real sovereignty because it owns nothing; assigning it control is merely a divine play, and alleged protectors have only the name of guardianship, like the spider’s house.
rows.anchor: فلما تولى بعض خلقه أمر بعض لم يكن ذلك منه ولاية حق لكونه لا يملك شيئا بحقيقة معنى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are singled out as beneficiaries of the sign even though it is generally available, because only they make use of it.
rows.anchor: تخصيص المؤمنين بالذكر مع عموم الآية لهم ولغيرهم لكون المنتفعين بها هم المؤمنون دون غيرهم

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting the fate of shirk and wrongdoing, the passage resumes with the command to recite revelation as a deterrent, through its proofs, stories, exhortations, warnings, promises, and threats; recitation deters both reader and listener.
rows.anchor: انتقل من ذلك - مستأنفا للكلام - إلى أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بتلاوة ما أوحي إليه من الكتاب

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer’s restraint is a natural tendency of its devotional form, not a complete cause that invariably prevents sin.
rows.anchor: السياق يشهد أن المراد بهذا النهي ردع طبيعة العمل عن الفحشاء والمنكر بنحو الاقتضاء دون العلية التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated prayer five times daily, especially in a sound community, trains a person away from major sins and other acts rejected by sound nature through instruction and practice.
rows.anchor: إذ أتى به العبد وهو يكرره كل يوم خمس مرات ويداوم عليه وخاصة إذا زاول عليه في مجتمع صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer teaches faith in divine unity, prophethood, and judgment; it trains sincere worship, dependence, seeking guidance, humility before God, praise, glorification, and regard for other righteous people.
rows.anchor: لقنه أولا بما فيه من الذكر الإيمان بوحدانيته تعالى والرسالة وجزاء يوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer also trains bodily and clothing purity, avoidance of impurity in clothing and place, and facing the House of God.
rows.anchor: مضافا إلى حمله إياه على التطهر من الحدث والخبث في بدنه والطهارة في لباسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a short period of prayer performed with some sincerity establishes a lasting disposition to avoid indecency and wrongdoing; no other program of self-training demands more.
rows.anchor: لو داوم على صلاته مدة يسيرة واستعمل في إقامتها بعض الصدق أثبت ذلك في نفسه ملكة الارتداع

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difficulty raised is that many worshippers commit grave sins and are not restrained by prayer.
rows.anchor: أنا كثيرا ما نجد من المصلين من لا يبالي ارتكاب الكبائر ولا يرتدع عن المنكرات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret prayer as supplication or a call to God’s command, which restrains people; al-Tabataba’i rejects this as departing from the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أن الصلاة في الآية بمعنى الدعاء والمراد الدعوة إلى أمر الله

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others take prayer generically to mean that some kinds or instances of prayer restrain from evil; the author says the context concerns prayer’s inherent effect, not only some instances.
rows.anchor: وذكر آخرون أن الصلاة في الآية في معنى النكرة والمعنى أن بعض أنواع الصلاة أو أفرادها

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say prayer restrains only while the worshipper is occupied in it; the author rejects this as too narrow for prayer’s lasting effect.
rows.anchor: وذكر قوم أن المراد نهيها عن الفحشاء والمنكر ما دامت قائمة والمصلي في صلاته

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some retain the literal sense but argue that prayer only admonishes without guaranteeing obedience, as with God’s command; the author says this mistakes restraint for necessary compulsion.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن الآية على ظاهرها والصلاة بمنزلة من ينهى ويقول لا تفعل كذا ولا تقترف كذا

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say prayer’s remembrance of God prevents disliked acts and at least reduces a worshipper’s wrongdoing; the author rejects making verbal remembrance alone the intended mechanism.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم في دفع الإشكال أن الصلاة تقام لذكر الله

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, prayer as worship creates a spiritual quality that tends to restrain the soul from indecency and sin; it does not merely describe a subset, the time spent praying, hearing a rebuke, or verbal remembrance alone.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به التوسل إلى ملكة الارتداع التي هي من آثار طبيعة الصلاة بنحو الاقتضاء

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a devotional orientation toward God whose restraining effect is dispositional, not inevitable; obstacles that weaken remembrance, presence, humility, and sincerity weaken that effect.
rows.anchor: فالحق في الجواب أن الردع أثر طبيعة الصلاة التي هي توجه خاص عبادي إلى الله سبحانه وهو بنحو الاقتضاء دون الاستيجاب

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the effect comparatively: people who abandon prayer often neglect other duties and lawful distinctions, while even minimal prayer restrains from many acts; greater care in prayer brings greater restraint.
rows.anchor: وجدته مرتدعا عن كثير مما يقترفه تارك الصلاة غير مكترث به ثم إذا قست إليه من هو فوقه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines remembrance first as a mental disposition for retaining acquired knowledge, distinguished from preservation by its emphasis on bringing knowledge to mind; he also uses it for presence in heart or speech.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الذكر تارة يقال ويراد به هيئة للنفس بها يمكن للإنسان أن يحفظ ما يقتنيه من المعرفة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes remembrance after forgetfulness from remembrance sustained without prior forgetting, and says any utterance can be called remembrance.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قيل الذكر ذكران ذكر عن نسيان وذكر لا عن نسيان بل عن إدامة الحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the original meaning to be inward remembrance; speech is named remembrance because it contains the inward meaning, with inward remembrance as the effect and intended end of verbal remembrance.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأصل في معناه هو المعنى الأول وتسمية اللفظ ذكرا إنما هو لاشتماله على المعنى القلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is called remembrance because it includes verbal declarations of God’s unity, praise, and transcendence, and because its total form embodies the servant’s worship of God.
rows.anchor: والصلاة تسمى ذكرا لاشتمالها على الأذكار القولية من تهليل وتحميد وتنزيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer produces remembrance as its end, as in the command to establish prayer for God’s remembrance; the intended remembrance is inward awareness, restored after absence or sustained continuously.
rows.anchor: والذكر الذي هو غاية مترتبة على الصلاة أعني الذكر القلبي بمعنى استحضار المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inward remembrance is the highest human work, the ultimate happiness prepared for humanity, and the key to every good.
rows.anchor: أفضل عمل يتصور صدوره عن الإنسان وأعلاه كعبا وأعظمه قدرا وأثرا فإنه السعادة الأخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, the phrase advances from prayer’s restraint of evil to its greater benefit: inward remembrance, prayer’s end, exceeds the partial good of restraint.
rows.anchor: ويكون المراد الذكر القلبي الذي يترتب على الصلاة ترتب الغاية على ذي الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two alternatives are that remembrance means the verbal remembrance contained in prayer or prayer itself as remembrance; either is greater than prayer’s restraining effect.
rows.anchor: ومن المحتمل أن يراد بالذكر ما تشتمل عليه الصلاة من الذكر أو نفس الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On both alternatives, remembrance is a genitive construction with the object as its complement, and the comparison is with restraint from indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: على الاحتمالين جميعا من المصدر المضاف إلى مفعوله والمفضل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited 2:152 supports the preceding reading that God remembers whoever remembers Him; the source then lists further interpretations of the phrase.
rows.anchor: البقرة 152، وقيل المعنى ذكر الله تعالى العبد أكبر من الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God’s remembrance of the servant is greater than prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى ذكر الله تعالى العبد أكبر من الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God’s remembrance of the servant is greater than everything.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر الله العبد أكبر من كل شيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the servant’s remembrance of God in prayer to be greater than the other pillars of prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله في الصلاة أكبر من سائر أركان الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says a servant’s remembrance of God in prayer is greater than remembrance outside prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله في الصلاة أكبر من ذكره خارج الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says a servant’s remembrance of God is greater than the servant’s other deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله أكبر من سائر أعماله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view interprets the phrase to mean that prayer is greater than the other acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى للصلاة أكبر من سائر الطاعات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says remembering God’s prohibition when facing indecency or wrongdoing is a stronger deterrent than prayer’s restraint.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله عند الفحشاء والمنكر وذكر نهيه عنهما أكبر من زجر الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view treats greater as non-comparative and needing no object, by analogy with the statement that what is with God is better than diversion.
rows.anchor: معرى من معنى التفضيل لا يحتاج إلى مفضل عليه كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author leaves these interpretations unexamined for brevity, while observing that the arbitrary character of some is apparent.
rows.anchor: فهذه أقوال لهم متفرقة أغمضنا عن البحث عما فيها إيثارا للاختصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows good and bad deeds; the verse urges watchfulness, especially under the first interpretation of remembrance.
rows.anchor: أي ما تفعلونه من خير أو شر فعليكم أن تراقبوه ولا تغفلوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ordering proclamation through recitation, the passage explains how to invite the People of the Book by setting rules for debate.
rows.anchor: بالتبليغ والدعوة من طريق تلاوة الكتاب عقبه ببيان كيفية الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted wording includes Jews and Christians, along with Zoroastrians and Sabians.
rows.anchor: وهم على ما يقتضيه الإطلاق اليهود والنصارى ويلحق بهم المجوس والصابئون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good debate avoids harshness, insult, and humiliation; gentle speech and a cooperative approach to establish truth make the exchange better still.
rows.anchor: فمن حسنها أن تقارن رفقا ولينا في القول لا يتأذى به الخصم وأن يقترب المجادل من خصمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception concerns opponents whom gentleness will not persuade, who instead treat it as humiliation or manipulation to divert them from their belief.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد بالظلم بقرينة السياق كون الخصم بحيث لا ينفعه الرفق واللين والاقتران في المطلوب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unattributed report characterizes the discerning scholar as one who understands God, acts obediently, and avoids divine displeasure.
rows.anchor: العالم الذي يعقل عن الله فعمل بطاعته واجتنب سخطه

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that prayer which does not restrain from evil only increases distance from God; al-Durr al-Manthur also transmits it via Imran ibn Husayn, Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Umar, and al-Qummi gives it as unconnected.
rows.anchor: روى أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say there is no prayer for one who does not obey it; obeying prayer means refraining from indecency and evil. Al-Durr al-Manthur also transmits this from Ibn Masud and others.
rows.anchor: وفيه وأيضا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that when told of a young Anṣārī who prayed with the Prophet yet committed immoral acts, the Prophet said his prayer would restrain him someday.
rows.anchor: وروى أنس أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي الصلوات مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah says one can judge whether prayer was accepted by seeing whether it restrained its worshipper from evil; acceptance is proportional to that restraint.
rows.anchor: روى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من أحب أن يعلم قبلت صلاته

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu al-Jarud transmits from Abu Ja'far that God’s remembrance of people who pray is greater than their remembrance of Him, as in the promise that God will remember those who remember Him; the author notes this is one previously listed interpretation.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report cited through Majma al-Bayan from Abu Abd Allah defines remembrance as remembering God in relation to what He permits and forbids.
rows.anchor: عن مجمع البيان وروى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ذكر الله عند ما أحل وحرم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: When Muadh ibn Jabal asked which deeds God loves most, the Prophet answered that one should die with the tongue moist from remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أي الأعمال أحب إلى الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the foremost are those who stay awake remembering God, and urges anyone wishing to graze in Paradise’s gardens to remember God often.
rows.anchor: وفيه وقال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kafi transmits from al-Abdi that Abu Abd Allah identifies the clear signs in the hearts of those given knowledge as the Imams.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن العبدي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imami identification is also reported through several chains in al-Kafi and Basa'ir; al-Tabataba'i calls it an application to the verse’s highest instances, supported by the next report.
rows.anchor: وهو من الجري بمعنى انطباق الآية على أكمل المصاديق بدليل الرواية الآتية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Buraid ibn Muawiya asked Abu Ja'far who the people given knowledge are; he answered that they are his interlocutors and asked who else could they be.
rows.anchor: وفي البصائر بإسناده عن بريد بن معاوية عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قلت له

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet condemns people who abandon their own prophet’s message for another prophet and community; this quotation follows the preceding segment’s report that Companions wrote Torah material and says this verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: إن أحمق الحمق وأضل الضلالة قوم رغبوا عما جاء به نبيهم إلى نبي غير نبيهم

rows.speaker: ابن مليكة
rows.claim: Ibn Asakir reports from Ibn Mulayka that Aisha returned a gift from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Kurayz, mistaking him for Ibn Umar and objecting that he pursued books; once corrected, she accepted it.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن عساكر عن ابن مليكة قال أهدى عبد الله بن عامر بن كريز إلى عائشة هدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the reports, especially the first, suggest this verse was revealed about some Companions, al-Tabataba'i says the surrounding context rules that out.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الروايتين وخاصة الأولى نزول الآية في بعض الصحابة وسياق الآيات يأبى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that many deny meeting God continues the verse’s astonishment; meeting means return to God in resurrection, and the wording heightens the wonder that creatures begin from Him yet do not end with Him.
rows.anchor: والمراد بلقاء الله هو الرجوع إليه في المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic particle signals that disbelief in resurrection is itself something that should be unbelievable.
rows.anchor: ولذلك أكده بإن إشارة إلى أن الكفر بالمعاد من شأنه في نفسه أن لا يصدق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of destroyed earlier peoples aims to make deniers of resurrection reconsider, since denial of the afterlife makes true religion pointless.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم حال الأمم الكافرة وما انتهت إليه من سوء العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stirring or turning the earth means turning it over for cultivation, reclamation, and similar purposes.
rows.anchor: وإثارة الأرض قلبها ظهرا البطن للحرث والتعمير ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wronging themselves refers to disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون } أي بالكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preferred parsing, al-sūʾā is kāna’s delayed subject and the predicate is advanced to restrict their end to that outcome; their evil deeds have no expressed object.
rows.anchor: قدم الخبر عليه لإفادة الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sūʾā means a condition that harms its possessor, here evil punishment; the following clause omits the causal lām, meaning punishment followed because they denied and mocked God’s signs.
rows.anchor: والسوآى الخلة التي يسوء صاحبها والمراد بها سوء العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense is that punishment was the final outcome of their wrongdoing because they denied and mocked the signs; this fits the passage’s warning.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ثم كان سوء العذاب هو الذي انتهى إليه أمر أولئك الذين عملوا السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses al-sūʾā as the object of their bad deeds and the denial clause as kāna’s predicate, so sins led to denial and mockery; the author says this sense is possible but unfitting here.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن { السوآى } مفعول لقوله { أساؤا } وخبر كان هو قوله { أن كذبوا } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse summarizes the proof: God originates and repeats creation, and all creatures return to Him; the plural return pronoun refers to the created beings.
rows.anchor: بعد ما ذكر الحجة وتكذيب كثير من الناس لخص القول في نتيجتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection criminals despair; iblās means despair of God and encompasses every misery.
rows.anchor: والإبلاس اليأس من الله وفيه كل الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters will find no intercessors among their supposed partners and will despair of them as well as of their deeds; in life they claimed their idols interceded with God, but they will disavow their worship.
rows.anchor: كما كانوا يقولون في الدنيا هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله وكانوا بعبادة شركائهم كافرين ساترين

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: The reports agree that Abu Bakr wagered with opponents on the Romans’ defeat and later victory, winning the stake at the Prophet’s indication; a report says the Prophet called the proceeds ill-gotten and told him to give them away.
rows.anchor: والذي تتفق فيه الروايات أنه قامرهم فقمرهم وكان القمار بإشارة من النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defense that the wager preceded the gambling ban fails: wine was forbidden from the beginning, wine and gambling are called sin in 2:219, and sin is prohibited by 7:33; al-A'raf is an early Meccan sūra, so the Prophet could not direct gambling.
rows.anchor: والإثم محرم بنص آية الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If gambling’s prohibition came only late, the Prophet’s reported judgment that the stake was ill-gotten and should be given away would still be inexplicable; juristic attempts to reconcile the account add difficulty.
rows.anchor: وعلى تقدير تأخر الحرمة إلى آخر عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يشكل قوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لأبي بكر لما أتى بالخطر إليه إنه سحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report’s claim that the Persians worshipped idols does not fit the author’s account: they were polytheists but did not adopt idols.
rows.anchor: ثم إن ما في الرواية أن الفرس كانوا عبدة الأوثان لا يوافق ما كان عليه القوم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits from Abu Ja'far that people see the immediate life of this world and deliberately overlook the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال يرون حاضر الدنيا ويتغافلون عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: When asked about the command to travel through the earth and observe, al-Sadiq answered that it means looking into the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فقال أو لم ينظروا في القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the people’s separation at resurrection as their division between Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي وقوله عز وجل { ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون } قال إلى الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the buyer of idle talk who misleads people and mocks revelation; waqr is a heavy load, and a load on the ears means something preventing hearing, though it is also said to be a metaphor for deafness.
rows.anchor: والوقر الحمل الثقيل والمراد بكون الوقر على أذنيه أن يشد عليهما ما يمنع من السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Qur'an is recited to this purchaser, he turns away arrogantly as if he had never heard it and were deaf, so he is threatened with painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وهو مستكبر كأن لم يسمعها قط كأنه أصم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One analysis explains the pronoun shifts as singular forms following the word-form of the relative, plural forms following its meaning, and then singular forms again.
rows.anchor: وقد أعيد إلى من يشتري ضمير الإفراد أولا كما في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author offers another possibility: the plural pronoun in the preceding verse refers jointly to the misleader and those misled, so pronouns referring to the relative can all remain singular.
rows.anchor: في الآية السابقة راجعا إلى مجموع المضل والضالين المدلول عليهم بالسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning the purchaser of idle talk, the passage returns to glad tidings and reassures believers with the lasting Garden promised by God.
rows.anchor: رجوع بعد إنذار ذاك المشتري وتهديده بالعذاب المهين ثم العذاب الأليم إلى تبشير المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the purchaser tries to make the Qur'an seem like false tales and treats its recitation arrogantly, the passage stresses God’s true promise, His might and wisdom, and His role as creator who may promise Paradise or punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما كان غرض من اشترى لهو الحديث أن يلتبس الأمر على من يضله بغير علم فيحسب القرآن من الأساطير الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As discussed under 13:2, the clause may be explanatory, meaning the heavens are seen without pillars, or restrictive, meaning they lack visible pillars and may have invisible supports.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون قيدا توضيحيا، والمعنى أنكم ترونها ولا أعمدة لها

words: وَأَلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed lofty mountains in the earth to keep it from shaking with its inhabitants; the wording suggests a direct relation between mountains and earthquakes.
rows.anchor: أي ألقى فيها جبالا شامخة لئلا تضطرب بكم وفيه إشعار بأن بين الجبال والزلازل رابطة مستقيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread across the earth every kind of animal that crawls upon it.
rows.anchor: أي نشر في الأرض من كل حيوان يدب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water sent down from the sky means rain, sent from above.
rows.anchor: أي وأنزلنا من جهة العلو ماء وهو المطر

words: فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noble pairs are kinds of plants that are fine, useful, and beneficial.
rows.anchor: وأنبتنا فيها شيئا من كل زوج نباتي شريف فيه منافع وله فوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to plant pairs alludes to pairing in plants, a subject discussed under a parallel passage.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى تزوج النبات وقد تقدم الكلام فيه في نظيره
